[43] concluded that since sulfide solid electrolytes have defects in their initial state, these initial defects can be further exacer- bated during battery cycling due to electrochemical-mechanical stresses induced by volume changes resulting from the embedding and de-embedding of lithium ions into the active material during charging and discharging. Therefore, these findings are consistent with our investigation that periodic pressure changes are a significant cause of cracking of the sulfide electrolyte.
